variants.label: M01
variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Design ONE NEW three-view RH JUNKER FREIGHTER variant. The user wants TWENTY genuinely different geometric designs at APPROXIMATELY HALF THE DETAIL DENSITY of IMAGE 1, the previous D-series. This sheet is one of those twenty. Think deeply about a concise, elegant ANGULAR INDUSTRIAL HULL SHAPE. Use a small number of substantial, well-fitted volumes with purposeful steps, cuts and one or two deep recesses. The design must look like an authentic Freelancer Rheinland freighter rebuilt by scavengers. The primary geometry and silhouette, not paint differences, distinguish this variant.

REFERENCE ROLES:
IMAGE 1: previous D-series freighter concept. Its dimensions, original cabin, high hump and mechanism remain useful, but it has TOO MANY hatches, grilles, repeated panel fields and nested outlines. Explicitly remove about half that visual subdivision. Freely recompose the main hull surfaces in the direction specified below; this is not a simple recolour or copying the same design with one removed vent. Keep meaningful medium-size depth and authored forms.
IMAGE 2: ACTUAL ORIGINAL RH pirate freighter, authoritative for ancestry and scale. Source flight bounds W 9.465, H 11.463, L 23.722; main cargo body about 6.3 wide, cockpit glazing about 3.6 wide. It is a tall, narrow cargo body with a raised hump, a low forward cabin and two rear engine modules. Stay near these overall proportions and original physical size. No fat transport, giant cargo pod, fighter or rounded ball.
IMAGE 3: IMMUTABLE original FREIGHTER cabin. Reuse its complete original appearance at unchanged size and position: sloping upper blue glazing, original pane divisions, opaque pale lower metal face with SEPARATE small rectangular blue window slots, narrow black/yellow trim, original chin and underside equipment block. Do not reshape, armour, cage or otherwise modify this cabin. No new cockpit, visor or continuous lower blue band. Fit all new hull transitions around the cabin; its real original geometry must be reused later.
IMAGE 4: close-up of the actually implemented RH pirate elite model, for construction quality only: well-seated recessed red panel fields, deep returns, thick closed hull surfaces and sharp plane changes. Transfer that practical craftsmanship, at restrained density. It does not authorize copying the elite's cockpit, wings, open frame or wheel.
IMAGE 5: the user's historical RH freighter concept art. Preserve the original's clear hierarchy of angular cargo mass, raised narrow hump, horizontal shoulders and separated compact propulsion. Its green paint and sketch cockpit do not replace the real pirate cabin in image 3. It reinforces clarity of form, not a primitive blockout aesthetic.

MEDIUM DETAIL BUDGET, roughly HALF of the previous D-series:
Make about 55-65 percent of visible hull area calm connected planes. Keep the design sophisticated through major geometry and a small number of meaningful medium-scale features. Replace clusters of small hatch panels with one larger designed donor hull field. Use approximately ONE large recessed cargo-door field per side, ONE smaller service recess, and ONE ventilation pocket where appropriate; do not repeat all three in every hull zone. The roof can have ONE substantial inset service/ventilation feature and a broad inset side field. A vent pocket has only THREE OR FOUR broad internal blades. Cylinder units get one substantial sliding collar and a simple inset endcap, not three concentric bezels, mini hatches and extra ring stacks. Each engine gets one meaningful shoulder transition, one service field and a clear exhaust lip. Do not keep every D-series panel, slot and lip just at smaller scale. No dense rivets, fine grid seams, tiny decals, dozens of bolts or uniform grunge. This is a visual target, not a numeric polygon budget.

GEOMETRIC QUALITY:
Develop four to six strong primary/secondary decisions in the hull profile, shoulder contour, lower cargo outline and hump interface. These MUST give this variant a distinct outline and volume balance. Keep crisp faceted wedges, stepped solid side housings, substantial closed-back recesses and well-joined donor sections. Preserve some actual relief and useful joints; do not reduce everything to an undecorated box with a roof cap. Continuous material around a recess is the hull itself, not an exterior decorative frame. At most a few broad donor sections can be physically offset or shaped differently. Subtle fixed-housing asymmetry is allowed when specified. Colour supports the geometry; it cannot be the main change.

SOURCE IDENTITY AND MECHANISMS:
Keep the prominent high RH freighter HUMP above a horizontal shoulder line, approximately the upper third of body height. It is a narrow closed cargo-roof arch built from broad authored facets, rising and falling fore and aft; not a huge dome, ball, exposed circular wheel or tiny low roof vent. Show enough substantial rectilinear cargo mass below it. The cabin connects through a short enclosed hull junction in its original position.
Each side has EXACTLY THREE retractable short closed-ended faceted CYLINDERS: large middle, smaller fore and aft, ONE row only. Six total. They extend laterally from thick solid hull cheeks, with simple sleeves and a plausible free withdrawal path. All three views show the SAME FLIGHT extension. Do not turn them into wheels, guns or side exhausts. Keep their main placements symmetrical even if fixed donor covers differ.
Two original-sized main engines at the AFT end, left/right at the SAME HEIGHT; use short CLOSED solid couplers. In true SIDE, their silhouettes overlap so ONE engine outline is visible. In TOP, show TWO separate engines. No third engine, vertically staggered pair or enormous bells.

HARD EXCLUSIONS:
NO exposed pipes, hoses, cables or conduits. NO exterior frame, truss, diagonal brace, cage, scaffold, separate ribs, hoops, straps, open rail or skeletal pylon. NO wings, fins, thin side paddles or claws/cranes. No random small machinery attached to the hull. No geometric rivets or tiny fastener fields. No uniform smoothing or rounded bevel on every edge. No integrated guns, turrets or missiles; a small empty flush equipment pad is acceptable. All exposed recesses have a closed back. Original cabin unchanged.

ART AND PAGE:
Refined Freelancer-era industrial concept art with confident ink edges and controlled marker/gouache plane shading on off-white paper. Restrained worn pale beige/grey hull, muted dark red recessed/donor fields, a little faded olive and dark cavities. Use sparse material wear, broad fields and only a few seam lines. Show an integrated dangerous scavenger craft, not a toy or glossy modern product. Landscape: large 3/4 front-side perspective on LEFT; true SIDE / FLIGHT upper right nose RIGHT; true TOP / FLIGHT lower right nose UP. Exactly three full uncropped views of the SAME design, same mass proportions, cabin, hump, panel locations and six cylinders. Technical views must be clear and consistent. All are flight pose. Only title specified below and the two view labels.

DISTINCT VARIANT ARCHITECTURE:
A tall central cargo block with matching large oblique cuts on its FRONT and REAR ends, creating a clear elongated six-sided side silhouette. The narrow raised faceted hump sits inside a continuous low shoulder ledge. Keep the side drum cheek one coherent blunt wedge, with a single large lower cargo recess and one compact service field. Both end cuts are primary hull planes, not bolt-on armour. Engine and original cabin joins stay short and closed.
Main title exactly: "RH JUNKER FREIGHTER / M01".
